newsitem.title: USA: C-Phone shrs up on quarterly order gains.
newsitem.headline: C-Phone shrs up on quarterly order gains.

text.p: Shares in C-Phone Corp traded sharply higher in unusually busy Nasdaq dealings, the buying stoked by C-Phone's recent announcement of a significant rise in new orders, traders said.

By midday Friday, shares in the Wilmington, N.C. maker of desktop video teleconferencing gear climbed 25 percent, or 1-1/4, to 6-1/2 after more than half a million shares traded, well beyond the 16,175-share average daily volume.
The gains came on top of yesterday's 1-1/2 point leap, appreciation of almost 42 percent, the Nasdaq's largest percentage gainer of the session.
Wednesday afternoon, C-Phone said that for the quarter ended August 31 it received record orders totaling $865,000 for its teleconferencing products, including associated software and installation.
About $670,000 of this will be recognized in the August 31 quarter and the balance will be recognized in the current quarter.
The August quarter results will be announced before October 15, the company said.
"Along with strong orders, the rate of use of our cash reserves has decreased as we move steadily towards profitability," company chairman Daniel Flohr said in a statement.
Telephone calls to the company seeking additional comment were unanswered.
For the three months ended May 31, sales were just over $400,000, up 13 percent from the prior-year period, while the company lost $0.20 per share versus a $0.42 per share loss.
In the fiscal year ended February 29, the company reported net sales of $1.8 million and a per share loss of $0.96 versus net sales of $945,035 in fiscal 1995 and a $1.03 per share loss.
Last month, the company changed its name to C-Phone from Target Technologies Inc.
